title: Microsoft Teams: Intelligent call delegation answers and screens incoming calls
summary: The briefing passes: its billing prerequisites, policy controls and rollout statements are supported by Microsoft documentation and the supplied notices. One minor correction is needed because the checklist names Auto-apply new services but the controls table does not cover that setting.

claims.claim: Intelligent call delegation is an AI-powered voice agent for Microsoft Teams calls.

claims.where: Scope: Users; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: MC1519860 says appropriately licensed users configure the feature under Call Settings, with options depending on admin configuration.
claims.quote: Once a user is provisioned with the appropriate licensing, users will be enabled to configure Intelligent call delegation under Call Settings.- Depending on admin configuration, users will have configuration options to personalize their intelligent delegate.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice identifies Personal attendant policies as the administrative configuration mechanism.
claims.quote: Admins will be enabled with Personal attendant policies that allow them to configure Intelligent call delegation settings for their users.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state the arrival behaviour for non-Frontier tenants without a spending policy beyond documenting the spending-policy prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: "Intelligent call delegation" "spending policy" "without". Read feature prerequisites and management sections, UBB overview and spending-policy guidance, and both supplied notices; none describes that non-Frontier arrival case.

claims.claim: The feature page does not further define which Microsoft Copilot licences count.
claims.quote: Searched: "Intelligent call delegation" "license" prerequisites. Read the entire feature page: its sole licence prerequisite is "Users must have a Microsoft Copilot license", without a plan or SKU breakdown.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions
claims.claim: Billing arrangements specifically at General Availability have not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Intelligent call delegation" "General Availability" "billing"; credits rate pricing. Read feature and UBB overview pages and both notices: preview billing is stated, but no GA-specific billing terms or change is stated.

claims.claim: The Learn feature page names recording and transcription controls but not their storage location.
claims.quote: Searched: "Intelligent call delegation" recordings transcripts stored access. Read the entire feature page and returned policy-setting excerpt; they describe automatic saving but give no storage location or access rules.

claims.claim: The usage-based billing overview lists Teams: Intelligent Call Delegation among supported services.
claims.quote:

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Limits; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A limited monthly budget limits the credits a spending policy can spend each month.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: Users who hit a spending-policy limit lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: Spending-policy credits reset on the first of the month.
claims.quote: until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.claim: The spending-policy page gives general guidance to set at least 2,000 credits per user per month.
claims.quote: Monthly budget limit for users: Set at least 2,000 credits per user per month

claims.claim: A spending policy uses prepaid credits before pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: The policy always uses prepaid credits first, whether through capacity packs or through pre-purchase plans, before moving to pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: Turning off Auto-apply new services prevents newly supported services from being automatically added to the spending policy.
claims.quote: When the setting is off, future services and agents aren't automatically included. Administrators must review and add the new services and agents to the policy.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center provides credit consumption monitoring against spending limits.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services
